summary: Compressed roughly 1.8x by splicing verbatim the opening, the water-gazing and Narcissus passages, the sailor-versus-passenger argument, the 'Who ain't a slave?' passage, the Fates' playbill and the closing whale-phantom, while cutting the artist/landscape illustration, the cook/broiled-fowl riff, the forecastle-air passage and the 'cannot tell why' Fates paragraph.
acceptable_changes: Cut illustrative landscape and artist material, which restates the water-and-meditation point already made by the retained examples.
Cut the cook/broiled-ibis digression and the old-family/schoolmaster elaboration within the narrator's self-justification; the retained lines keep his comic self-deprecating voice.
All retained text is verbatim source with only whole-sentence cuts, so no connective prose was invented.
risks: Chapter runs somewhat over the 1200-word target to protect signature material (opening paragraph, Narcissus, Who ain't a slave, closing image).
Whole-sentence cuts inside the 'passenger' and 'sailor' paragraphs slightly thin the catalogue of offices and indignities.
The 'being paid' paragraph is reduced to its punchline; the money-as-root-of-ills irony is partly lost.
review_focus: Check that the paragraph beginning 'But wherefore it was...' still reads smoothly after the forecastle-air sentences were cut.
Confirm the opening paragraph and Narcissus passage are intact verbatim, as the likely signature passages.
